sentences.text: Hello and welcome to the Slow English podcast.
My name is Emilie and today we're going to learn about Mexico City.
Mexico City is the capital of Mexico.
It is one of the largest cities in the world.
More than 20 million people live in Mexico City and the area around it.
That is a lot of people.
The city is very busy, very colorful and always full of life.
The history Mexico City has a very long history.
Many, many years ago before the Spanish arrived, the city was called Tenochtitlan.
It was built by the Aztecs in the 14th century.
The Aztecs built the city on a lake.
They made islands called Chinampas where they grew food.
In the 16th century the Spanish conquistadors came.
They destroyed Tenochtitlan and built a new city on top of it.
That city became Mexico City.
Because of this the city has two stories.
The Aztec past and the Spanish colonial history.
Famous places.
One of the most important places in Mexico City is the Zocalo, the main square.
The Zocalo is very large.
Around the Zocalo you can see the Metropolitan Cathedral and the National Palace.
The National Palace has many beautiful murals painted by Diego Rivera, a famous Mexican artist.
Another special place is the Chapotepec Park.
This park is huge.
It is bigger than Central Park in New York.
In Chapotepec you can walk, relax, and visit museums.
Inside the park there is the Chapotepec Castle which is the only royal castle in North America.
Mexico City also has the National Museum of Anthropology.
This museum is one of the most important in the world.
You can see the Aztec sunstone, statues, and objects from ancient cultures like the Maya and the Olmec.
Art and culture.
Art is everywhere in Mexico City.
The artist Frida Kahlo was born here.
She lived in a bright blue house called Casa Azul.
Today her house is a museum.
People can visit and see her paintings, her clothes, and the rooms where she lived.
Diego Rivera, her husband, was also a famous painter.
He painted big murals that show the life of Mexican people, their work, and their struggles.
His murals are in schools, palaces, and museums all around the city.
Music is also very important in Mexico City.
You can hear mariachi music in plazas and restaurants.
Mariachi bands wear special clothes, play guitars, violins, and trumpets, and sing about love, history, and Mexico.
Food Mexico City is famous for its food.
People eat tacos, quesadillas, enchiladas, and tamales.
You can buy food in small restaurants, but also in the streets.
Street food is very popular.
You can try tacos al pastor, made with pork, pineapple, and onion.
You can also drink horchata, a sweet rice drink, or a toli, a warm drink made with corn.
And for dessert, many people enjoy churros with chocolate.
Food is more than eating.
It is part of Mexican family and culture.
People often eat together with family and friends, and meals are a time to share stories and laugh.
Every day life Mexico City is very big, so people use the metro to travel.
The metro is one of the largest systems in the world.
Millions of people use it every day.
The tickets are very cheap.
Each station has a symbol, so even people who cannot read can know where to go.
The city is high in the mountains, more than 2,200 meters above sea level.
That is higher than many cities in the world.
Because of this, the weather is cooler than you may expect.
Sometimes the air is thin, and some visitors need time to get used to it.
Mexico City is also full of markets.
The most famous one is La Merced Market.
You can buy fruit, vegetables, clothes, toys, and more.
Another famous market is Mercado de Coyoacán, where you can try traditional snacks and see colorful crafts.
Traditions and celebrations.
Mexican people love festivals.
In Mexico City, you can see big celebrations.
One of the most famous is the Day of the Dead in November.
People make altars with flowers, candles, photos, and food to remember their family members who have died.
The streets are full of decorations, and people paint their faces like skeletons.
Another big celebration is Independence Day on September 16.
The President of Mexico gives the famous Grito de Dolores from the balcony of the National Palace in the Zocalo.
Thousands of people come to the square to celebrate with fireworks, music, and flags.
People, the people of Mexico City are friendly and warm.
They are proud of their culture, their history, and their traditions.
Life in the city can be busy, but people enjoy spending time with family, eating together, listening to music, and celebrating special days.
Conclusion.
So now you know about Mexico City, its history, its museums, its art, its food, and its people.
It is a city of life, color, and tradition.
Thank you for listening to the Slow English Podcast.
I am Emily.
